notes: Correct fix that adds constant-folding of concatenated literal names, which is more precise than the reference but extra complexity, and a small interface abstraction. Its tests are the most thorough: request-only GET/POST, ph() retry, transport-error retry still allowed, and an integration test.

The fix is correct and slightly more precise than the reference, because it folds constant string concatenations so only truly evaluation-time names count as dynamic, but the placeholderReporter interface and the folding helper add abstraction the task did not need; tests are the most thorough, covering a large classification table, GET and POST end-to-end runs, ph() retries, transport-error retries still allowed, and an integration test.

Correct AST-based fix exposed through a predicate-style ReferencesPlaceholder API. It also treats unadapted `rp.*` names as response placeholders, which the spec does not ask for and which is a slight deviation, though mostly harmless. Tests are strong (unit table, handler regression, integration), with some comment churn on an existing test.

AST collection matches the reference and the predicate-based ReferencesPlaceholder API is clean, but isResponsePlaceholder also accepts a speculative raw 'rp.' prefix that never exists at runtime; tests are strong (classification table, end-to-end body check, integration test) and it correctly rewrites the comments of the existing is_transport_error test.

Essentially the same design as the reference, with a member-function guard and clear docs. Handler-level tests cover request-only cases (upstream.host, lookalike, escaped) and response cases (status, status_text, ph(), dynamic, latency). The latency test relies on a sleep, and two request-only subcases would not have retried even before the fix.

It matches the reference: at provision time it walks the checked CEL AST for ph() calls, flags non-literal names as dynamic, and checks the collected names against an exact response-placeholder list plus the header prefix; tests cover the request-only variants end-to-end and response retries including latency, ph(), and dynamic names, though the escaped and status_codes cases would not have retried even before the fix.

Closely mirrors the reference: it collects placeholder names from the checked AST, flags non-literal names as dynamic, and uses an exact-name-or-header-prefix check in a tight helper. Tests cover all the maintainer-specified cases, plus an end-to-end regression and a direct ph() retry.

It is a near-reference implementation that reuses isCELCaddyPlaceholderCall and isCELStringLiteral and keeps a small, focused helper in reverseproxy; tests cover classification including mixed matcher sets, the POST body regression, and ph() retries, but there is no end-to-end check for the upstream.host case.

Correctly implements skip/notice and --links exposure for both backends, keeps List and NewObject naming in agreement, and also resolves collisions between a symlink and a real `x.rclonelink` member; it adds strong tests (squashfs binary fixture, copy and escape tests) plus a fitting docs section.

Matches the reference semantics in both backends: List and NewObject agree, the --links notice names the flag, and range/seek are clamped; it also makes a regular `.rclonelink` member win over a colliding symlink, and its tests are thorough (zip, squashfs testdata, copy and escape).

The main zip and squashfs symlink paths work, but the zip root handling is convoluted and gives the wrong name to a symlink whose real name ends in .rclonelink when a root is set; it also adds unrequested behaviour (a new exported ErrLinksNeedsSuffix, a `dt[""]` root hack, keeping parent dirs of skipped links visible, an odd ErrorIsFile with empty listing for an unsuffixed root without --links), though the tests are extensive.

Works and tests well, but adds a lot beyond the task: a new shared ErrLinksNeedsSuffix, `dt[""]` seeding, parent-dir retention for skipped links and an odd squashfs stat fallback; the zip root logic trims and re-adds the suffix and drops it for suffix-named symlinks under a root.

Works for ordinary symlinks, but the zip side never appends the suffix to a symlink whose own name already ends in .rclonelink, breaking the name-plus-suffix convention; squashfs silently yields an empty target if the stat type mismatches, and its squashfs tests skip when mksquashfs is absent.

Core behaviour is right, but the zip side skips the suffix for symlinks whose names already end in `.rclonelink` (unlike its squashfs side), squashfs silently uses an empty target when stat info is missing, NewObject lookup is spread over three functions, and squashfs tests need mksquashfs.

Clean implementation for both backends: List and NewObject agree, regular .rclonelink members stay regular, and a symlink whose name ends in .rclonelink still gets the suffix; it leniently accepts a root with or without the suffix, has a minor typed-nil return pattern, and its squashfs tests depend on mksquashfs.
Clean implementation with consistent List/NewObject naming, symlinks always suffixed and a lenient root accepting either name; the squashfs tests depend on mksquashfs and may be skipped.
